_: Main story beats (see docs/STORY.md and scripts/story.gd). %hero %pet %town %partner are filled in. A beat fires once; 'after' names a beat that must have fired first.

penguins.title: Chapter 1 — The Day the Star Crystal Came Down
penguins.summary: Something fell in your field and asked for help. The sky went red. Two brave penguins touched it.

lines.text: %town. Cobbles, a fountain that works on Tuesdays, a bell tower whose bell hasn't rung in twenty-one years, not since its clapper split in two, and penguins at the edge of everything: on the walls, in the doorways, one asleep on the fountain. The island's old families. Nobody minds.
Everyone looks up when you pass, and then very carefully looks somewhere else. A town that has been waiting for something to happen for a long time, and isn't sure it wants it to.

effects.hint: Talk to everyone once. Maple sells seeds; Gideon fixes tools; the penguins keep to themselves, mostly.

lines.text: The sky over the east meadow goes a dark, dark red. Lightning, with no thunder after it. Then a howl: not a wolf. Lower, and sadder, and somehow angrier for being sad.
Oh no. They've come for the power. I hoped we'd have longer.
You wanted to farm in peace. I wanted that for you too. I'm sorry: they didn't wait.
Still think I'm a rock? Rocks don't get frightened, farmer. Listen to me anyway.

Listen, farmer. That's the Grumps, the army I told you about. They followed me here. He has felt me land. I've put a bubble over this farm; nothing of his can cross the fence after dark. But the meadow is outside the bubble, and so is the town.

I passed over this island once before, farmer, twenty-one years ago, running, with his army on my heels. The sky went red then too. Your town's bell cried out when they went over, so hard its clapper split. I'm sorry for that. This time I'm not running.
Wooden sword, warm heart, east gate. And farmer: they weren't always Grumps. I'd rather show you than tell you.

effects.hint: The howling is in the east meadow. The farm is safe after dark; nothing else is.

lines.text: Where the Big Grump stood, the grass comes back green in a circle. The last of the grey shakes off like water, and out of it rises a small crystal, no bigger than a plum, glowing a shy pale blue. It turns once in the air, as if to look at you, and floats away east toward the stars. In the grass where it was: a collar. Leather, chewed, a brass tag worn smooth. BISCUIT. For one cold second you think of %pet. No: the tag is old.
You look at the glowing thing in your field, far behind you, for a long moment. It isn't a rock. You've known that for a while.

That was one of my people. A crystal of Crystopia, my home, where every crystal sang. The Dark Crystal doesn't make Grumps. He talks to us, sweetly, promising paradise, until we believe him. And then we forget who we were.

Most of his Grumps were crystals once. Not all: some he picked up on the way, and the grey sticks to them too. That collar's dog is still out there somewhere, shaggy and grey and lost. Maybe not forever.
The rest isn't mine to tell. It's a sad story, and there's someone who tells it better than I do, with a hundred cats listening.

They can be turned back. Not beaten down: turned back. There's a magic for it, the Meow Pow Wow, and I only carry the first spark of it. The ones who truly know it are the cats of Cat-topia, on Celestica. Her world touches yours at the crystal meadow, past the big one; the rings over it are hers. I can hear them purring from here. We go there next.
The town doesn't know any of this. They think the meadow has wolves.
choice: Tell the town what the Grumps are.
Keep it quiet. They've got enough to worry about.

0.text: Brave. They'll look at every stray dog differently now. That might be good. It might be very hard.

1.text: Kind. And lonely. You'll be carrying it, then. I'll carry it with you.

0.hint: The town knows what Grumps are now. Alder will want to talk.

1.hint: You keep it to yourself. Maple can tell something's wrong. The collar is in your pack.

quest: cattopia
Find the purring in the crystal meadow: talk to Catkins by the cat statue.

lines.text: So the wolves were never wolves. ...I've been shooing them off my step with a broom for a month. Someone's dog, Theo says. Someone's something.
I'll tell the others gently. You go and find whoever can turn them back.

effects.hint: Alder is telling the town, gently. Catkins, in the crystal meadow, can teach you to turn Grumps back.

lines.text: You came back from the meadow with a dog collar and a face like a closed shop. I won't ask.
...If you ever need a counter to lean on, mine's here.

penguins.title: Chapter 2 — Cat-topia
penguins.summary: The voice in the crystal meadow. Catkins teaches the Meow Pow Wow. The cave shakes.

lines.text: On the road east %partner stops walking. Then stops touching the ground. No penguin has ever flown before; %partner flies the whole last stretch, laughing, trailing rainbows, and pulls you up by the sleeve toward a ringed world hanging low over the meadow. Far behind, over the island, a second rainbow answers.

On the road east, two small shapes pass high overhead, trailing rainbows: the penguins, flying, though no penguin has ever flown before. They loop once over you, laughing, and one peels off back toward the island. You walk the last stretch toward a ringed world hanging low over the meadow.

On the road east you stop walking. Then you stop touching the ground. No penguin has ever flown before; you fly the whole last stretch, laughing, trailing rainbows, toward a ringed world hanging low over the meadow. Far behind, over the island, a second rainbow answers.

The crystal meadow. Purple and green, and rings of light turning slowly over it: Celestica's rings, seen from underneath. Where the Star Crystal landed, the sky went thin, and here your valley touches her world. Past the standing stones, a mountain with a mouth, and a fog coming out of it.
A thread of the Star Crystal's light has come along, riding on your shoulder like a spark that forgot to go out. Back home, the rest of her keeps the bubble over the farm.
And purring. Definitely purring. A dark figure walks out of the fog, takes down its hood, and is a cat.

Welcome to Cat-topia, farmer, and to the brave two, wherever they are standing tonight. I can feel them both from here. We're happy you survived the army of the Grumps. Come inside; it's warm, and it's time to learn your powers.

effects.hint: Talk to Catkins, by the cat statue in the crystal meadow.

lines.text: Inside it's warm. Cat treats everywhere, scratching posts, a hundred cats, and some of them flying. Nobody mentions the flying.
My name is Catkins, leader of Cat-topia. Keeper of the Paw, the old ones call it. There has always been a Catkins; I am the latest, and I have been the latest for a long, long time.

Around the hall, cats sit in rows on round cushions, eyes half shut, breathing together. The flying ones hang still in the air, like they're listening. Catkins turns to the spark of starlight on your shoulder, and bows, very low.
Teacher.
You were a kitten the last time I came this way. You fell asleep in my light, and I didn't have the heart to move you.

Three thousand years ago she sat where you are sitting and taught the first of us. My line has kept the Meow Pow Wow ever since. We don't fight with it; we breathe with it. Stone, water, wind and fire, moving through the heart. Sit. All of you sit; this is the sad part.

Long, long ago the star crystals understood that everyone needs love and happiness. They made worlds where everyone had everything they needed. But one of them thought the most important thing was power. He began to control the others, and made them join the Grump army.

The Grumps want to take away all the love and happiness in the universe. He talks the crystals of Crystopia grey until they forget themselves, and then anyone they touch. That's a Grump: not a monster. Somebody, squeezed.
The only hope is to use the secret power of the star crystals against him. The Meow Pow Wow. It melts a grumpy heart, and the Grump remembers love and happiness, and helps us.
Breathe in, slow, like a mountain would. Hands make a heart at your chest. Hold it. Rainbow hearts and cat paws will fly out of you. Try. ...Yes. YES. A-meow-zing.

Use it near a Grump and it turns back into what it was before he talked it grey: a crystal of Crystopia, most of the time, flying home. Sometimes a rabbit or a frog he picked up on the way. Little ones first. It grows as you grow, and as your friends do.
And the penguin who walks with you, and the one keeping watch: that warm hum they've been feeling since they touched her? Now they know how to let it out too.
And you, little one: that warm hum you've felt since you touched her? Now you know how to let it out.
Something warm goes out of your chest in colours you don't have names for. Across the cave a very old cat stops frowning for the first time in years.

quest: spark

Build the Crystal Resonator from the Plans board by your house (10 stone, 1 shard), then refine 3 shards into a Refined Crystal in it. Shards: the meadow boss, mountain rocks, the beach wreck, the mine's crystal floors.
effects.toast: Meow Pow Wow learned: tap ♥ near a Grump to turn it back. Your partner can use it too now.

lines.text: You dream you're standing on a floor that breathes. Somewhere, something enormous beats, slow, like a heart that's been asleep a long while. The mountain's heart. You've never heard its name, but in the dream you know it: Prismatica.

A voice, not the Star Crystal's. Older. "They keep digging. Let them; every floor they open, the mountain hears. But the heart is not under it. The heart is at the very top, where the mountain touches the sky."
You wake with grit under your fingernails. %pet is sitting up, staring at the floorboards.

effects.hint: The mine is the inside of the mountain. The heart it dreams about is at the very top.

lines.text: There. The second spark. It's small, but it's yours, and it's the first new spark in a very long time that didn't come from me or from Catkins' line.
The Refined Crystal is still warm in your hand when the purring from the east stops. All at once. You run. By the time you reach the crystal meadow, Catkins is in the cave mouth, waving you in.
Then the cave shakes. Crystals fall from the ceiling. Catkins meows loudly.
The Grumps have found our sacred cave. They know we're the only ones left with the magic to stop them. RUN. The catship is this way.
A ship shaped like an enormous cat, ears and all. Everyone aboard. The Grump ships are on its tail before it clears the meadow.
Don't worry. We have prepared for this. We have a very powerful secret weapon. Prepare the catapults, kitties.

The cats load the catapults with LITTER BOXES. Everyone holds their nose. %pet sneezes three times. The stink hits the Grump ships; they can't see; they crash, one after another, into the dark Wastes past the meadow.

The cats load the catapults with LITTER BOXES. You hold a flipper over your beak. %pet sneezes three times. The stink hits the Grump ships; they can't see; they crash, one after another, into the dark Wastes past the meadow.

A-meow-zing! We've bought some time. Their Commander is down there in the Wastes. He was a person once. When you're ready, farmer: the Wastes gate opens for someone who can hold a sword like they mean it.
The catship circles once over the Wastes, purring like an engine, and sets you down by the meadow's east gate. The cats wave from every window. Some of them wave from outside the windows, flying.

And after him, it is up to the two of you. Go to the heart of Crystopia: Mount Prismatica. Here at the meadow your valley touches my world; past the Wastes it touches theirs, and you can walk the rest. Only at its heart can you master the Meow Pow Wow. I wish you two luck.

quest: wastes_gate
Reach Combat 3, then face the Grump Commander in the Wastes (east gate of the crystal meadow).
effects.toast: Litter Box: throw it; every Grump nearby stops to hold its nose.
effects.hint: Litter boxes stun Grumps. Catkins sells more in the crystal meadow.

lines.text: Last night you woke at midnight and found the two penguins on the fence, looking up at Celestica's rings.
Catkins said it melts a grumpy heart. One heart. But if it melts one, it can melt every one. Not just beating him: whole kingdoms where everyone's happy. Everywhere. The whole universe.
That's a lot of kingdoms.
Then we'd better start soon.
Then I'll carry the snacks. And help. Mostly help. Some snacks.
Pip-Pip chirps, once, softly. It sounds like yes.
Last night you woke at midnight and couldn't get back to sleep. Pip-Pip was already on the fence, looking up at Celestica's rings. You climbed up beside him.
You've got your thinking face. The big one.
You told him: Catkins said it melts one grumpy heart. But if it melts one, it can melt every one. Whole kingdoms where everyone's happy. The whole universe.
That's a lot of kingdoms. ...Then I'll carry the snacks. And help. Mostly help. Some snacks.
Last night you woke at midnight. Nova was on the fence, looking up at Celestica's rings. You climbed up beside her.
Catkins said it melts a grumpy heart. One heart. But if it melts one, it can melt every one. Not just beating him: whole kingdoms where everyone's happy. Everywhere. The whole universe.
That's a lot of kingdoms, you told her. You chirped it, mostly.
Then we'd better start soon. You carry the snacks.
The smoke clears. On the grey ground, where the Commander stood: a brass locket on a snapped chain. Inside, two boys on a dock, one holding a fish too big for him.
You know that dock. It's the lake. The smaller boy has Finn's ears.
...Oh. He went to the river cities, didn't he. Everyone who goes there comes back changed. The Dark Crystal has a man there in a grey suit. I've felt him. I don't know his name.
The locket is warm. It hums very faintly, like it's trying to remember a tune.
choice: Keep it. It's humming; that means something.

0.text: Yes. Whatever it costs him to hear it, he should hear it from someone who was there.

1.text: It's crystal-touched. It will know its own kind when it meets it. Don't lose it.

0.hint: Take the locket to Finn in town.

1.hint: The locket stays in your pack, humming to itself.

quest: sky_stair
First the mountain pass (the crystal babies) and a night's camp, then the great tree in the forest: the way up Mount Prismatica starts above the clouds.

lines.text: You hold out the locket. Finn doesn't take it. He looks at it the way you'd look at a wave that's going to hit you anyway.
Tomas. My brother. That's... that's the pike. He never caught anything bigger. Told everyone he did. Where did you—
No. Don't. I know where. I knew when he stopped writing. ...But there's no him in it, is there? Just the locket. Then he's still out there. Then he can still come home.
He'll like you. He likes anybody who'll walk into a field and swing at what's howling. Keep swinging, %hero. For both of us, yeah?
He takes the locket then, and turns toward the water so you won't see his face. You give him the quiet, and look at the lake too.

effects.hint: Finn knows now. He took the locket, and he's glad it was you who brought it.

lines.text: In your pack, the brass locket starts to hum, loud enough to hear. Down on the jetty, Tomas turns his head toward the sound like someone hearing his name across a field.
You kept it. ...Good. Give it to him, not me. It's his.
Tomas holds it a long time. Then he opens it, and laughs, once, at the size of the pike.

penguins.title: Chapter 3 — Mount Prismatica
penguins.summary: Big Jim's campfire. The crystal babies. Coldy and the sacred key. A knight above the clouds.

lines.text: Mount Prismatica, the heart of Crystopia. Catkins sent you here, and now you see why nobody comes. So tall the top is in space, and no ship can fly it; the magic won't allow it. It has to be climbed on foot.
The light on the rock changes as you watch: pink, then purple, then orange, then green. It gets colder every ten steps. The penguins don't mind. Anyone else does.

effects.hint: Climb. The pass is blocked by something small and loud.

lines.text: That night, by the farm gate, something comes down the lane after you, all the way from the mountain path. Bushes. Footsteps. The penguins press close together. Out of the shadows jumps a large figure.
It's just me. It's Big Jim. I couldn't let you do this alone. I brought camp gear.

A fire in your own yard. Marshmallows. Shooting stars. An aurora the colour of the inside of a crystal, and Big Jim in a heavy winter coat, saying the next days will be the hardest: mysteries to solve, and things in the hills that don't want you to pass.

That night, by the farm gate, you build a fire in your own yard and wait. Bushes. Footsteps. It's only the wind; the penguins laugh at you for jumping. Marshmallows, shooting stars, and you in your heavy winter coat, telling them the next days will be the hardest.
I kept watch over the island while you were in Cat-topia. The red sky goes to that mountain every night, and comes back a little bigger.
I kept watch over the island while you were in Cat-topia. The red sky goes to that mountain every night, and comes back a little bigger. Also I ate the snacks.
Also I'm not carrying the litter boxes. I want that said now.

effects.hint: Big Jim tags along on the climb (he doesn't fight), and both penguins can come now: switch partners in Party. If the crystal babies still hold the pass, turn them back with ♥.

hint_hero.big_jim: Both penguins can come on the climb now: switch partners in Party. If the crystal babies still hold the pass, turn them back with ♥.
hint_hero.penguin_f: Big Jim tags along on the climb (he doesn't fight), and Pip-Pip can come too: switch partners in Party. If the crystal babies still hold the pass, turn them back with ♥.

lines.text: Round the corner: a baby girl, two feet tall, covered in crystals, angry, silent. Then she stamps. STAMP. STAMP. STAMP. And chants, deafeningly: BEE BOP BOO BABY. BEE BOP BOO BABY.
By Jove. That baby looks like she's made of crystals.
From every cave on every side: stamp, stamp, stamp. Hundreds of them pour out and block the path, and the leader GROWS, to five feet, and the circle closes. There's no room to run.
First guardians of the mountain, I'd say. How do we get past them?
The leader holds up her hand. Silence. She steps forward and asks, very seriously: "Bee bop boo baby?"
The penguins look at each other for a long while, and then chirp at her. She looks delighted.
Oh. Oh, I see. They've been cursed by the Dark Crystal: all they can say is that. You can understand them because of the magic. And you're going to lift it. The Meow Pow Wow.

effects.toast: Don't just fight them: tap ♥ (Meow Pow Wow) when they're low.
effects.hint: The babies are cursed, not evil. Turn them back with the Meow Pow Wow (tap the ♥ button).

lines.text: The spell can be seen from space. The crystals of the mountain make it brighter. A flash of white, and when the colours settle, the baby leader steps forward with a smile.

The spell can be seen from space. The crystals of the mountain make it brighter. A flash of white, and when the colours settle, the other babies step back and look at you: their leader, yourself again.
You saved us babies! ...What bring you to Mountain?
The penguins chirp for some time. She nods.
Yes. I understand. You come to improve Meow Pow Wow so you get big, strong, and save universe. We babies know you are good. We allow you to pass.
But I must come with you. I hold the sacred key to the heart of Mount Prismatica. And...

0.text: (whispering) There are secret spies of the Dark Crystal in these hills. Finargles. Very sneaky. You may need help.

1.text: Coldy. That is my real name. Babies call me Leader. You call me Coldy. ...There are spies in these hills. Finargles. Very sneaky. We go quiet.

lines.text: The penguins chirp for some time. The babies stamp, once, all together: thank you. The sacred key to the heart of Mount Prismatica is warm in your hand, and the way up is yours to show them. There are finargles in these hills. You go quiet.

effects.hint: Coldy joined. She carries the sacred key to the heart of Mount Prismatica. Up: the great tree, then above the clouds.

lines.text: Above the clouds it is very quiet, and the islands float like they've forgotten what holding on is for. It's dark up here even at noon; the stars are out.
We are surrounded. The finargles are here.
The shadows between the islands have grown thicker. Something black and fuzzy, the size of a large pumpkin, with two eyes and no mouth, watches you from each one. None of them blink.
On the far island, a figure in blue-white armour, perfectly still. Frost on its shoulders with the same pattern as the frost on your gate the morning the penguins came.
That's a penguin, farmer. Or was. Older than the brave two put together. The Dark Crystal doesn't only make Grumps; sometimes he makes guards.

effects.hint: Finargles: purple eye-light dazes you. The Crystal Knight on the far island; Nova would know him.

hint_hero.penguin_f: Finargles: purple eye-light dazes you. The Crystal Knight on the far island. You know that shape.

lines.text: You dream of purple eyes in a dark room, and a crown that isn't there yet.
*So you are the ones. You are smaller than he said.*
Bad dream? Finargle dream. They walk in sleep. Coldy stamps on them for you.
...Grandfather Auk. He swam out after the red sky the night the bell broke, before we hatched, and climbed the mountain alone. They said the mountain took him.
...Grandad? Nova. Nova, that's Grandad.
The mountain didn't. It was this. I can feel him in there, under the glass. The Meow Pow Wow reaches bigger things every time I use it. I don't know if it reaches that big.
The Knight turns its head. Slowly. Toward Nova, not you.
choice: Let Nova try the Meow Pow Wow first.

0.text: Keep him off me for ten seconds. That's all. Ten.
She makes the heart at her chest, and the clouds go still to listen.

1.text: ...Right. Crack that armour open, then, and get him out of there.

0.hint: Tap ♥ near the Knight when he's below a third of his strength: Nova's Meow Pow Wow.

lines.text: Grandfather Auk. He swam out after the red sky the night the bell broke, before you hatched, and climbed the mountain alone. They said the mountain took him.
The mountain didn't. You can feel him in there, under the glass.
The Knight turns its head. Slowly. Toward you.
choice: Try the Meow Pow Wow on him.

0.text: Keep him off you for ten seconds. That's all you need. You make the heart at your chest, and the clouds go still to listen.

1.text: Crack that armour open, then, and get him out of there.

0.hint: Tap ♥ near the Knight when he's below a third of his strength: your Meow Pow Wow.

lines.text: In the last of the glass, before it melts, a face. Old, tired, not unkind. It says one thing, so quietly the clouds nearly take it:
A man in a grey suit bargains with him. Under the river cities. He thinks he's winning.
A man, choosing it. That's worse, farmer. That's much worse.

quest: teleporter
The top of the mountain is in space. Power the moon teleporter with 3 Refined Crystals, then face the spire.
effects.hint: Something with purple eyes has been watching from the shadows. Stay sharp up here. (The moon teleporter on the mountain pad will need 3 Refined Crystals.)

lines.text: He heard me. At the end. I don't know if that's better. I think it's better.
When we go up there, to the heart: he'll be there. I don't know how I know. I know.
He heard you. At the end. You think that's better. And when you go up there, to the heart, he'll be there. You don't know how you know.
Among the shards, one that doesn't melt. Warm, heavy, and when you pick it up your sword hand stops aching.
Nova kneels by a line of small webbed footprints leading up into the cloud. 'He ran. He's still in there somewhere. I'll find him.'
You kneel by a line of small webbed footprints leading up into the cloud. He ran. He's still in there. You'll find him.

effects.toast: Knight's Shard: your sword hits harder.

penguins.title: Chapter 4 — The Finargles and the Merkitties
penguins.summary: A crystal prison. A question in your head. The uphill stream, the waterfall, and the song that gives you a tail.

lines.text: You don't see it happen. A small black shape in a crack of shadow; purple light from two eyes; and you can't move a muscle. A flash. And you are somewhere else: a room of crystal, no door, and your friends beside you, blinking.
We are caught by very powerful finargles. Most finargles do not have those abilities until they are teenagers. At least ten thousand years old.
*Who are you, and why do you climb Mount Prismatica?*
They are telepathic. They talk in our minds. They have no mouths.
That one is Fennimore. Strongest finargle on the mountain. Mountain has had no queen since the old one went quiet. She wants the crown.

*I am Fennimore. The Dark Crystal has promised me I will be queen of this mountain once he has defeated the Two Too Powerful Penguins. He says he wants to make the universe a perfect paradise. Why do you fight him?*
choice: Tell her the truth: what he does to the ones he promises things to.
Tell her nothing. Look for a way out.

0.text: The penguins chirp for a long time. Silence. Then: *The Dark Crystal said you would lie to me about him. I will not be deceived.* ...But the voice is slower than it was, and it doesn't come back for a while.

1.text: *Very soon the Dark Crystal will be told that I have you.* The voice goes. The room is very quiet.

lines.text: Floor. We drill. Meow Pow Wow at the floor; the mountain listens to it.

The spell goes down instead of out, and the crystal under you goes soft, and then it isn't there. You fall into fast dark water that carries you UP, through the mountain, for what feels like hours, everyone holding hands. Big Jim: "I see a light!" And then you are in open air, and falling, down a waterfall, into a jungle, into a pool, into black.

The spell goes down instead of out, and the crystal under you goes soft, and then it isn't there. You fall into fast dark water that carries you UP, through the mountain, for what feels like hours, everyone holding hands. Someone shouts "I see a light!" It's you. And then you are in open air, and falling, down a waterfall, into a jungle, into a pool, into black.

effects.hint: You washed out at the lake. Someone pulled you from the water.

lines.text: You wake on the shore with the sun going down, and no idea how you got out of the water. A blue-green glow comes toward you across the shallows: a cat with a long fish's tail, wearing a glowing necklace.
You wake on the shore with the sun going down. A blue-green glow in the shallows: your own people, the merkitties, come to find you.
Oh good. You've all woken. We found you after the waterfall; you were in a bad way. We've been hiding you. The finargles have been through here looking for you, so we've made you invisible to them.

More glows in the water. Merkitties. One of them: "Mer, the finargles have told the Dark Crystal. The Grumps are coming to the mountain, and the whole surface is swarming with spies looking for our new friends."

Then we share our merkitty magic. With it, every water is a road: the under-mountain tunnels come up under the old landing pad, whenever you're ready. From there the moon teleporter goes the rest of the way, to the very top. Everyone into the pool.
I don't know about that. What do these muscly catfish want to do to us?

Everyone into the pool. The merkitties swim a circle around you, singing, and their necklaces glow, and all at once you have a tail. Mer: "You can become a mermaid now, any time you enter water." Big Jim screams. He screams for some time. Everyone wears earplugs until he stops.

Everyone into the pool. The merkitties swim a circle around you, singing, and their necklaces glow, and all at once you have a tail. Mer: "You can become a mermaid now, any time you enter water." You scream. You scream for some time. Everyone wears earplugs until you stop.

Everyone into the pool. Your people swim a circle around your friends, singing, and the necklaces glow, and all at once they have tails. You tell them: any water, any time. Big Jim screams. He screams for some time.

effects.toast: The merkitties' gift: you grow a tail in any water. Swim anywhere.
effects.hint: You can swim and dive anywhere now. The way to the top is the mountain pad: the moon teleporter needs 3 Refined Crystals.

lines.text: Every shadow between the islands has eyes in it again. Then the eyes part, politely, and one pair comes forward: bigger, and ringed with a faint purple light, like a crown that hasn't been made yet.
*You escaped my prison. Nobody has ever escaped my prison.*
Nobody escaped because nobody was in it before. Is new prison.
*...It is a very good prison.*
*He has not answered me since I told him I had you. Not once. Is that what he does, after?*
*Go on, then. Climb. He is waiting at the top, and so am I.*
The eyes close, one pair at a time, until the shadows are only shadows.
You dream of a grey, very small finargle sitting on your windowsill, so old its fuzz has gone white at the edges.
*I am the oldest of us on the mountain. I remember the last queen. She sang to the mountain, and the mountain sang back.*
*Fennimore wants the mountain to sing to her. That is not the same thing. Someone should tell her, kindly. We have no mouths; we were never good at kindly.*
In the morning there is a single white tuft of fuzz on the sill. %pet sniffs it and sneezes.

effects.hint: Fennimore is listening. If she doubts the Dark Crystal, the Meow Pow Wow can turn her back at the top.

lines.text: It remembers where it goes. So do I. I wasn't sure I would.

Before we go: your town's bell. It hasn't rung since the night I fell past it. Alder would know what it needs. A town that rings its bell is a town that's awake, and the Dark Crystal has never once beaten a town that was awake.
Not an order. A hope. Go home first, farmer. Sleep. Say goodbye to the field like you'll see it again, because you will.

quest: alder_gold
The town bell's clapper split the night the red sky went over. Bring Alder a gold bar for a new one.
effects.hint: The bell needs a new clapper: a gold bar for Alder (optional). When you're ready: the moon (mountain pad), then touch the crystal spire.

lines.text: The bell rings. Twenty-one years of silence, since the night the red sky went over, come off it in one note, and the note goes out over the fields and the lake and the mine and comes back smaller and nicer.
My father pulled this rope. Everyone's in the plaza. Everyone. I didn't tell them to come.
You didn't have to. That's what a bell is for.
They know what's out there now. They came anyway. That's the part I'll put in the records.
Maple catches your eye across the plaza and nods once. Two people in this crowd knew why the bell matters. Now it's the whole town.
That bell broke for me. Now it rings for you.

effects.hint: The bell rang, and the whole town came to the plaza. (If the fight on the moon is still ahead, they will remember it there.)

lines.text: Morning. Frost on the gate again, though it isn't the season for it. %partner is waiting there, and so, a little apart, is whoever else still counts you a friend.
Top of Mountain. In space. Coldy never go to space. Coldy bring hat.
The top. Grandfather went up there alone. We won't.
Space. Is there food in space? I packed food for space.
No water on the moon. I asked. I'm coming anyway.
Space! I wore the big coat. I'm wearing it in space.
Nobody says anything for a while. Nobody needs to.
The pad on the mountain goes to the moon: that IS the top, farmer; the mountain reaches that far. The crystal spire, right there on the moon. That's where he is. That's where he's always been.
%pet barks once, at nothing, the way dogs do when they've decided.

effects.hint: Mountain pad → moon → the crystal spire (just north of the teleporter).

penguins.title: Chapter 5 — The Heart of Mount Prismatica
penguins.summary: The spire is the Dark Crystal. The finargle queen stands with him. Whatever you kept, and whoever you kept, comes with you.

lines.text: The spire isn't a spire. It's a crystal the size of a church, grown out of the top of the mountain where it pierces the sky, and it is dark the way a closed eye is dark.
Coldy holds up the sacred key. The crystal doesn't have a door, until it does: a dark seam opens like an eye.
You hold up the sacred key. The crystal doesn't have a door, until it does: a dark seam opens like an eye.
The sacred key goes still in your pack, humming, like it knows this place.
Sister. You brought a FARMER. And the two little birds.
I brought friends. You remember those. You had some.

I remember being left. I remember every kind thing, and how little it weighed when it mattered. Power weighs. The man in the grey suit knows it. The one who would be queen of this mountain knows it. So will you.

*I told you he would come,* says a voice in your head, and a black fuzzy shape the size of a pumpkin rises beside the dark, crowned in purple light. Fennimore. The ground shivers. Shapes pull themselves out of the dark like they've been waiting for their cue.
*...You said he squeezes the ones he promises things to.* The purple light around Fennimore flickers. *I have been promised things.*
She's listening, farmer. Turn her back, don't break her. She'll remember.

effects.toast: Fennimore hesitates: she can be turned back with the Meow Pow Wow.

lines.text: From very far away, carried on nothing at all: a bell. One note, twenty-one years of rust, and then voices under it. The whole town, in the plaza, saying your name.
...What is that. What IS that.
That's weight. The kind you forgot.

effects.toast: The Dark Crystal's shell cracks: it's half as strong.

lines.text: On the ridge, frost glowing blue-white on his feathers, an old penguin who stands taller than he should. Grandfather Auk. He doesn't fight. He stands between the shards and Nova, and the shards won't go near him.

On the ridge, frost glowing blue-white on his feathers, an old penguin who stands taller than he should. Grandfather Auk. He stands between the shards and you, and the shards won't go near him. "Grandfather," you say.
Grandfather.
Told you he'd come. I didn't tell you. I'm telling you now.
I owe you a sky, little one. Go on.

effects.toast: Grandfather Auk holds the shards off.

lines.text: A rose-gold light comes up the ridge, and Grandmother Brine with it, cartwheeling the last few steps.
Said I'd come, dear. Eight hundred and twelve, and still the first one here. Mind your feet.

effects.toast: Grandmother Brine's coral light: you're healed.

lines.text: A green glow, and Old Tidewhisker, juggling three pearls up the slope without dropping one.
The tide comes in for friends. It comes in even up here. Especially up here.

effects.toast: Tidewhisker's tide wears at the Dark Crystal.

lines.text: Frost-blue light, and Captain Icewhisker, who climbs the spire's own shadow like a mast.
Shards don't like the cold. Watch.

effects.toast: Icewhisker freezes the shards.

lines.text: An ember glow, and Lady Cinderpaw, barefoot on the cold glass, laughing at it.
Sing, darlings. All four verses. He hates singing.

effects.toast: Cinderpaw's starfire scorches the dark.

lines.text: And beside the crystal, in the dark, %bitter. They don't look at you. You did that, a long time ago now, at a gate.
You see? Everyone you leave comes to me. Everyone.

effects.toast: %bitter stands with the Dark Crystal.

lines.text: It stops. Not dead; stopped, the way a held breath is stopped. In the cracks, something flickers that isn't dark.
Pieces are missing from it. Clean breaks, like someone has been chipping splinters off and carrying them away, down toward the city.
Now. While it's quiet. Farmer: the Meow Pow Wow. The real one, the one Catkins meant. Hands at your chest. It's been in you since the cave.

choice: Make the heart. Turn him back.
Break the dark. Let it end.

0.text: You put your hands at your chest, and you think about the collar, and the locket, and the bell, and the gate, and the babies stamping, and Big Jim screaming about tails, and rainbow hearts and cat paws come out of you so bright they can see them from the island.

You put your hands at your chest, and you think about the collar, and the locket, and the bell, and the gate, and the babies stamping, and your own screaming about tails, which you'd rather not remember, and rainbow hearts and cat paws come out of you so bright they can see them from the island.
The dark goes grey. The grey goes glass. The glass goes bright, bright, BRIGHT — and there are two crystals on the top of the mountain, and they are both crying, if crystals can.
...Sister. I'm so tired.
I know. Come home. There's a field.
One heart. Then every heart. That's how it starts.
In your pack, the locket goes warm, then hot, and hums a whole tune at last. Far below, down toward the river cities, something hums back.
*...Oh,* says a small voice in your head, and the purple light around Fennimore goes out, and she is just a fuzzy black thing the size of a pumpkin, blinking, with no mouth to say sorry.
Up on the ridge, the elders' four lights brighten together, and for a moment the whole mountain sings.
Up on the ridge, the elders' lights brighten together, and for a moment the whole mountain sings.
Where %bitter stood, someone sits down hard on the glass, blinking, grey draining out of them like rain off a coat. "...I don't remember walking here," they say. "I remember the gate."
The ones he squeezed are still out there, farmer. They'll be easier to reach now. And the man in the grey suit will feel this. Let him. That's someone else's story now.
You called me a talking rock, the day I fell. Look at you now.
You only wanted to farm in peace. Go and do it. You earned it.

1.text: You let the light go the other way. The dark comes apart the way ice goes on a pond in spring: all at once, and then quietly, for a long time.
...That was my brother. He isn't, right now. But he was, and maybe one day he will be again.
No new Grumps will come. The ones still out there have to be turned back one by one, and I think you know how. The man in the grey suit won't stop. But that's a different story, and someone else's.
Where %bitter stood, someone sits down hard on the glass, blinking, grey draining out of them like rain off a coat. "...I don't remember walking here," they say. "I remember the gate."
You called me a talking rock, the day I fell. Look at you now.

effects.hint: Go home. Sleep. See what the morning says.

lines.text: Morning. The field. The Star Crystal is in the middle of it, half-buried, like she's been planted. She has.
Beside her, smaller, a second crystal, pale and quiet, still getting used to the light.
I asked him where he wanted to be. He said: somewhere things grow. I said I knew a place.
The pieces of him went out like sparks, every which way. Maybe one day they'll find each other again. Until then, I planted myself somewhere things grow. Somebody should.

At the gate, a dog. Old, grey at the muzzle, a brass tag worn smooth. It looks at the house like it's been away a long time and isn't sure of its welcome. %pet runs to it, and the two of them sniff each other all over, tails going.
The collar in your pack fits him exactly. You know whose crusts he's been following.
A letter on the step, in a hand Finn will know: "Coming home. Don't let him tell it about the pike. —T."

On the fence, two penguins, brother and sister, watching the sun come up over the island the way they must have watched the crystal come down. One of them chirps. You're fairly sure it means: what's next?
You sit on the fence beside the other penguin, watching the sun come up over the island the way you watched the crystal come down. You chirp. It means: what's next?
The first kingdom of happiness. Here. Then the next valley. Then everywhere.
There's always another chapter. But not today. Today there's turnips.

effects.toast: Thank you for playing. The farm goes on.
effects.hint: The story is done. The merkitty islands, the mine's deep floors and the green planet past the station are still out there.

lines.text: Posy sees the dog before she sees you. The paper bag of crusts falls out of her hands.
Biscuit? ...BISCUIT.
He's grey. He's so grey. Where has he— no. I don't care. He came back.

effects.hint: Biscuit is home with Posy. He still visits %pet.

gangsters.title: Chapter 1 — Lie Low
gangsters.summary: A deed with the wrong name. A letter. Somebody already knows.

lines.text: %town. The kind of place where nobody asks your name because they've already decided what it is.

A store, a smith, a clinic, a town hall with a bell tower and no bell. A man with a bad knee who watches the road the way you watch it, from the bridge in the morning and the bench by the south gate after lunch. Sal.

effects.hint: Sal (the bridge in the morning, the south-gate bench after lunch) has been places. Maple sells seeds and asks no questions.

lines.text: The President's man stumbles off between the rocks and is gone, leaving his coat behind. In it, a photograph of your old front door, and a phone with one number in it.
You don't call it. You think about it for a long time, and then you don't.
Written on the back of the photograph, in a hand with hard loops on the W and a hard press on the K: "WE KNOW ABOUT THE FARM. NICE TOUCH."
choice: Hold it up to what you remember of the first note.

0.text: Ash in the meadow grass. Let them wonder.

1.text: It goes in with the deed. Paper keeps. Paper remembers.

2.text: Hard loops on the W, a hard press on the K. You'll know that hand the next time you see it.

quest: hideout
Get through the gate to Hideout town and find a place to work from.
effects.hint: Tell Sal (the bench by the town gate) about the President's man. The Hideout gate is past the meadow, east through the outskirts.

lines.text: That was the President's man in the meadow. Not a good one, but one of his. You sent him running.
I used to run with a crew in the river cities, before. If you're building something... I'm in. Call it rent.
Hideout town. Past the outskirts, through a gate that doesn't look like a gate. Deuce does card tricks there, Mama Rosa feeds whoever's left, nobody runs the street. That's the opening.
You'll want people. Not thugs; those are a crystal a dozen. People. Ones who want something you can give them.
And boss? The President doesn't send one man. He sends one man, and then he sends the weather.

effects.hint: Hideout town: Deuce (card tricks), Mama Rosa (kitchen door). Recruit people, not thugs.

gangsters.title: Chapter 2 — The Hideout
gangsters.summary: A town that isn't on maps. Two recruits. A shop, if you want one, and what it costs.

lines.text: Up close it smells of the diner's burnt coffee, and somebody has painted a crown on the drive-in screen. Everybody here came from somewhere they can't go back to, which makes you a local.
A man at a folding table doing card tricks for nobody. A woman in a doorway with a rolling pin and an expression. Two people who want something.

effects.hint: Deuce at his folding table; Mama Rosa at the kitchen door. Each wants something before they'll join.

lines.text: Sit. No? Then stand, it's your knees. I'm Deuce. I do card tricks, I don't cheat, which is why I'm here and not uptown.
You're building something. I can tell; you've got the look of someone counting. I'm in, for a fee. A hundred and fifty, or catch my best card trick, one try, and I'll waive it.

0.text: Cash. Boring. Effective. Welcome to the crew, boss; I'll keep the books.

1.text: He fans the deck and your card vanishes. He does it again, slower, and you watch his left thumb, and you call it.
...You watched the thumb. Nobody watches the thumb. Fine. FINE. I'm in, and I'm never doing that one for you again.

lines.text: You're thin. Everyone who comes through that gate is thin. I had a kitchen in the river cities that fed forty men a night and none of them ever said thank you, and then it burned.
Bring me ten of anything you grew with your own hands. Ten. Then we'll talk about whose crew I'm cooking for.

0.text: She weighs each one in her hand like it might be lying.
...Dirt under the nails. All right, farmer. I'm in. Somebody in this crew is going to eat properly.

1.text: The door's open. It's always open. That's the problem with it.

lines.text: Boss. The bakery in %town. Woman who runs it is sweet, and the lease is a joke, and the back room has a door onto the alley.
An arcade there pays the crew for a season. She'd have to go, of course. Somewhere nice. We'd make sure.
choice: No. Not her shop. Not anyone's.

0.text: That's the counting look. I like the counting look. I'll send the boys with a polite letter.
Three days later, the bakery is boarded, and there's a man in a good coat on the avenue at night who nods when you pass.

1.text: ...Huh. All right. I've worked for worse reasons. We'll make money the slow way; I hear it keeps.

0.hint: Posy's bakery is an arcade now. A thug walks the avenue at night.

quest: docks
The docks move everything. Take them from the dock boss.

gangsters.title: Chapter 3 — The Docks
gangsters.summary: Crates with purple crystals in them. Three recruits. A fence with an offer.

lines.text: Every crate on the manifest goes to the same place: UPTOWN, TOWER, SUB-BASEMENT 3.
He isn't moving money. He's moving something that eats money, and luck, and whole towns. You've seen the colour before. In the meadow, in the thing that was his man.
Someone who can read a manifest like a map would be worth a lot right now. The girl with the laptop in the warehouse doorway hasn't looked up once. She's looked up three times.

effects.hint: Specs (warehouse door) wants the manifest. Ladder is up the crane. Halo races on the dock road.

lines.text: Don't say anything. Give me the paper. ...Yes. YES. Sub-basement three. I knew it had a basement. Buildings like that always have a basement.
I'm Specs. I'm in. I was in before you got here; I just hadn't told you. Keep the paper, I've got it memorised. Don't lose the paper.

effects.toast: Specs joined the crew.

lines.text: From up here you can see the whole dock, the whole road, and about a third of the tower. I've been counting trucks. Four hundred and twelve.
I don't fight. I see. You want someone who sees, I'm yours. You want someone who fights, ask the twins; they're always looking for a reason.

effects.toast: Ladder joined the crew.
effects.hint: Ladder counts trucks. He'll warn you before a raid.

lines.text: Race you. Dock road, end to end, your legs against my car. I'll give you the first fifty yards because I'm a gentleman.
You don't win. Nobody wins against Halo. But you don't stop, either, and when she pulls up at the end you're still coming, and she watches you come.
Most people quit at the containers. I drive for people who don't quit at the containers. I'm in.

effects.toast: Halo joined the crew.
effects.hint: Halo can drive you between the gangster districts (talk to her at the hideout).

lines.text: You're the farmer with the paper. Don't look surprised; it's my business to know who has paper. I'm Marlene. I buy things people shouldn't have.
A letter, in a certain hand, with a certain W. There are people who'd pay to have it not exist. Two thousand. Tonight.
choice: Sell it. ◆2000 buys a lot of crew.

0.text: Sensible. Paper is only worth what someone fears it for. ...He'll know your face by the weekend, you understand. That's the price under the price.

1.text: Then it's worth more than two thousand, and you know it. Keep it dry. I'm in, by the way. I like someone who knows what they're holding.

0.hint: The President knows your face now.

quest: neon
Put out Flame in the neon district.

lines.text: You're the farmer with the paper. Don't look surprised; it's my business to know who has paper. I'm Marlene. I buy things people shouldn't have.
A letter, in a certain hand, with a certain W. There are people who'd pay to have it not exist. Two thousand. Tonight.
choice: Sell it. ◆2000 buys a lot of crew.

0.text: Sensible. Paper is only worth what someone fears it for. ...He'll know your face by the weekend, you understand. That's the price under the price.

1.text: Then it's worth more than two thousand, and you know it. Keep it dry. I'm in, by the way. I like someone who knows what they're holding.

0.hint: The President knows your face now.

quest: neon
Put out Flame in the neon district.

lines.text: You're the farmer who had the paper. Don't look surprised; it's my business to know who has paper. I'm Marlene. I buy things people shouldn't have.
There was a letter, in a certain hand, with a certain W. People would have paid to have it not exist. Then I hear you burned it on your first night.
So you're the only person in this city with nothing to sell me. I find that... restful. I'm in. Somebody should fence for you who isn't an idiot.

effects.toast: Marlene joined the crew.

lines.text: You're the farmer with the paper. The tower's open now, so whatever that paper was worth, nobody's buying.
Nothing left to sell me. I find that restful. I'm in. Somebody should fence for you who isn't an idiot.

effects.toast: Marlene joined the crew.

gangsters.title: Chapter 4 — Neon
gangsters.summary: A dragon sign, a pit under the street, and six more who might follow you.

lines.text: Neon. Rain that's pink on one side of the street and blue on the other. Under the dragon sign, a woman who sets things on fire for a living, and a crowd pretending not to watch her do it.
Down a stairwell with no sign: the sound of a crowd that isn't pretending anything.

effects.hint: Flame under the dragon sign. The pit is down the unmarked stairs.

lines.text: At the edge of the crowd, a pair of identical faces in red and blue stop clapping first and look at each other.
Pit's open.
We fight the winner.
We ARE the winner.
That's what I said.

quest: pit
Win the fight pit under the neon street.
effects.hint: The twins fight in the pit. Dice owes the pawnbroker for a busted scooter; the Kid lost his board; Doc wants herbs; Sasha is the ring's muscle.

lines.text: ...Okay.
Okay.
We're in. Both of us. You don't get one.
Nobody gets one.

effects.toast: Vic and Val joined the crew.

lines.text: I'm not— look, I run things. Messages. Small things. I borrowed the pawnbroker's scooter and I wrecked it. Three hundred to fix, and he's started saying my name in a voice.
Clear it and I'm yours. I'm fast and I'm scared and both of those are useful.
choice: Go have a word with the pawnbroker.

0.text: You— just like that? Boss. BOSS. Okay. Okay okay okay. I'm in.

1.text: The pawnbroker is a man at a counter under a bare bulb, winding and rewinding a watch he never sells. You don't say anything. You put your hand flat on the counter, and you leave it there, and after a while he nods.
What did you SAY to him? He gave me my dice back. He never gives anything back.

lines.text: No. No, I know who you are, your face is on a— he's got your FACE, man. I run messages. I'm not running yours.
He's gone before you can answer. Marlene did say there was a price under the price.
The hood doesn't move. After a while a hand comes out of it and makes a shape: a board, wheels, gone.
Flame's guys took it. Under the dragon. It's got a sticker of a cat.
Under the dragon sign, in a pile of what used to be Flame's things: a board with a cat sticker. You bring it back. The hood nods once, which you're told later is a speech.

effects.toast: The Kid joined the crew.

lines.text: Sit. Let me see that arm. ...You hold a sword like a hoe. That's not an insult; hoes are honest.
I patched people for a man uptown, once. I stopped. Bring me five wild herbs from the forest and I'll patch for you instead, and I'll do it properly.

0.text: Good roots. Good. I'm in, boss. Try not to need me.

1.text: I'll be here. I'm always here.

lines.text: You beat the champion. The champion was soft. I'm the one who carries the champion out.
I don't join. I follow. Walk out of here and don't look back to see if I'm coming, and we'll both find out.
You walk out. You don't look back. At the top of the stairs, a shadow the size of a doorway falls over yours.

effects.toast: Sasha follows the crew.

lines.text: The arcade's doing great, boss. The painter's studio next door — Lumi? — has room for a second floor of games. She'd land on her feet. Painters do.

0.text: Lumi leaves on the morning bus with a canvas under each arm and doesn't look at the arcade. Two men in good coats on the avenue now.

1.text: You're a soft touch for a boss. I keep forgetting I like that.

lines.text: Last one. The clinic. I know. I KNOW. But we could run it, and the woman there — Juniper — she's been sending letters to the capital about us, boss. I read them.

0.text: Juniper doesn't leave quietly. She stands in the plaza and says what you are, to everyone, and then she goes. The bell tower stays empty. Nobody would pull the rope for you now.

1.text: ...Good. I was hoping you'd say that. Don't tell the boys.

gangsters.title: Chapter 5 — Uptown
gangsters.summary: The tower. The doors. The man with the stone in his chest.

lines.text: The doors are brass and twelve feet tall and have a slot in them like a mailbox. You know what goes in the slot. You've known since the rain.
The letter goes in. Somewhere inside, a mechanism that has been waiting for exactly this paper, this hand, this W, turns over once.
The doors open. Nobody fights you. That was the point of keeping it.

effects.hint: The doors are open. The lobby.

lines.text: The doors are brass and twelve feet tall and have a slot in them like a mailbox. The letter has been folded into the deed since the rain.
It goes in. Somewhere inside, a mechanism turns over once, and the doors open. Nobody fights you.

effects.hint: The doors are open. The lobby.

lines.text: The doors are brass and twelve feet tall and have a slot in them like a mailbox. The letter is still in your coat, read so many times it's soft.
It goes in. Somewhere inside, a mechanism turns over once, and the doors open. Nobody fights you.

effects.hint: The doors are open. The lobby.

lines.text: Stand back. I used to clean these doors. The service lock still takes my old key.
A click, a sigh of brass, and the tower doors swing in without a sound.

effects.hint: The lobby is quiet. Nobody knows you're in.

lines.text: Brass, twelve feet tall, a slot like a mailbox. Whatever was supposed to go in it, you don't have it any more.
Move.
Your crew put their shoulders to the brass together, and the mechanism inside gives with a sound like a bell that's been dropped.
Every light in the tower comes on at once. So much for quiet.

effects.hint: The lobby. They know you're coming.

lines.text: The lobby is marble and very, very cold. At the far end, a man in a grey suit in a chair that is too big for him, and in his chest, where a pocket square should be, a purple stone the size of a fist, pulsing.
He turns the chair. You know the face. You've known it longer than you've known your own name: the man who got you out of the city with a coat over your head and a deed in your pocket.
Hello, kid. You read my letters. Burned, kept, memorised: I wrote every one of them so you'd do exactly what you did. M. was always me.
The note on the envelope, the hard loops on the W? My other hand. You only ever saw me write with the right. I made sure of that.
I put your hands on that deed. I sent the man with the photograph so you'd be angry enough to climb my stairs. And here you are. You always did come when I called.
Twenty-one years ago a star fell in your field. I took one piece and left the rest under the soil, waiting for someone it would trust. It trusts you. I made sure of that, too.
You met my young people on the way up. I gave each of them a splinter of this, one black stone pressed into a cold hand on a bad day. Every Gift in this city is the same stone, and the stone is mine.
It promised me nobody would ever leave me again. Everybody leaves, kid. So I stopped needing anyone to stay. Come and see what that buys.
I've got the patching up, boss. You've got him. Remember what I said.

effects.toast: Doc patches you up mid-fight.

lines.text: He's on his knees on the marble. The stone in his chest is cracked and dark and it's whispering, and you realise you've been hearing it since the meadow.
Take it. The city. The chair. You've earned it; you counted every step. Put your hand on the stone and keep counting.

choice: Pull the stone out of him.
Put your hand on it. Take the city.

0.text: It comes loose with a sound like a cork. He gasps, once, and then he's just an old man in a bad suit on a cold floor, looking at his hands like they're new.
...I was going to come out to the farm. One spring. Help you plant, and tell you all of it. It said I didn't need to. It said you'd come to me.
You put the stone on the marble and you break it with your heel, and the whisper stops, and somewhere above the city a very old bell that was never going to ring again rings once anyway.
All over the city the splinters go quiet. A girl on the docks watches the flame in her palm gutter, and then, slowly, come back smaller, and steadier, and hers.
The Gifts stay. They are only what they always were underneath: ten young people who were told a stone made them worth something, finding out it was the other way round.

1.text: It's warm. That's the surprise. It's warm, and it's grateful, and it's got so many plans.
Later, in the chair, you write a letter to someone who's gone to ground on a farm. You tell them the farm is a nice touch. You notice, as you seal it, the hard loops on the W.
Across the city, ten splinters warm in ten pockets, and ten young people turn toward the tower without knowing why. They work for you now. They always did work for the stone.

effects.hint: Go home and sleep. The crew will be at the gate in the morning.

lines.text: Morning. Rain again, the collar kind. The deed on the table still has the wrong name on it, and you find you don't mind; names are things you can grow into.
At the gate, the crew. All of them, the ones who stayed, leaning on the gate like they've been there since before the sun. Sal at the front.
Boss. Word's all over town by now. They're not sure what you are. Neither am I.
Doesn't have to be decided today. We'll mind the farm. Somebody's got to water the turnips.

effects.toast: Thank you for playing. The farm goes on.
effects.hint: The story is done. The farm, the crew and every block you haven't walked yet are still yours.
